core_obligations: Reduce to connected U (proof lines 10955-10961): for an etale U over X, properties of etale morphisms decompose U into connected smooth curves mapping to X, and the sequence for U is a product of those for the pieces, so it suffices to treat U connected and hence irreducible.

Identify the displayed sequence (proof lines 10961-10980): the author recalls the exact sequence 1 -> Gamma(U, O_U^*) -> k(U)^* -> direct sum of Z over the points of U, rewrites it as a sequence of sections of the sheaves appearing in the statement, and concludes that the maps are the ones in the Fundamental Exact Sequence and that exactness holds except possibly at the last step.

Surjectivity (proof lines 10981-10985): to see surjectivity the author recalls that a divisor on a nonsingular curve is Zariski locally principal, which produces a local section mapping to a given element.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a connected etale U over X, where the classical sequence applies.
Identify the classical sequence with the sequence of sections of the sheaves in the statement.
Use that divisors on a nonsingular curve are locally principal to obtain surjectivity.
difficulty_reason: The theorem states the fundamental exact sequence of etale sheaves on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field (statement lines 10943-10953, with the set-up delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 10937-10941). The proof reduces to a connected etale U over X, where the sequence for U is a product of the sequences for the components (proof lines 10955-10961), identifies the classical exact sequence of the structure sheaf, its units and the divisor group with the sequence of sections of the sheaves in the statement (proof lines 10961-10980), and then uses that divisors on a nonsingular curve are Zariski locally principal to obtain surjectivity (proof lines 10981-10985). The non-formal content is the identification of the classical sequence with the sequence of sections; the final surjectivity step is indicated by the author through the locally principal property of divisors and is retained verbatim inside the counted span.
